topic: dsh-vision-router: Eyes for Text-Only DeepSeek Harness Agents

key_points: Vision routing plugin for DeepSeek Harness (DSH) that gives text-only agents eyes: keeps Host-canonical image pixels on the vision model's side and DeepSeek on the reasoning side.
One-command install via `npx @deepseek-ai/dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-vision-router`; ships its own composition patch (dsh.bundle.patch) so no manual file edits.
Free by default: built-in keyless OVHcloud anonymous fallback chain (5 models, ~2 req/min per IP per model, ~10 RPM across buckets); user-provided vision models run first.
No Python: pipeline (downscale, grounding, crop, pixel diff, palette, OCR, SVG trace, cutout, HTML screenshot) runs on sharp / potrace / tesseract / system Chrome.

14 deep vision tools: vision_describe, vision_ground, vision_detect, vision_crop, vision_present, vision_pixel_diff, vision_colors, vision_ocr, vision_trace, vision_extract_foreground, vision_html_screenshot, vision_screenshot (opt-in), vision_long_screenshot_ocr, vision_bootstrap.

Image memory: vision answers cached by attachment content hash; later text turns substitute the recorded description (marked untrusted evidence) so DeepSeek remembers earlier images without re-spending vision calls.
DeepSeek stays the brain; vision model is only the eyes. Text turns untouched in model, cost, context.
v2.1.5 verified against DSH 0.1.5-alpha.1; stable Host support through 0.1.2-rc.1; Node >= 22.
DSH Hub catalog entry: 1093 GitHub stars, updated 2026-09-09, category UI/Vision.
Install: `npx @deepseek-ai/dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-vision-router`, then restart `dsh web`.
Image turns work like ordinary tool-calling turns; paste an image to use it.
Vision requests use user-provided vision models first, then built-in keyless OVHcloud fallback chain.
Sandbox test passed: installed in a fresh profile and registered into the harness profile; executes shell commands; no obvious pitfalls found.
Image tiles pass through model gates and a lens, producing crops, pixel comparisons, traced contours and screenshots.
Uses agent/request waterfalls and bundled dsh.bundle.patch to add a composition row, admission wrapper and attachment limits.
Poor fit where the harness already provides the required vision route, or where external anonymous endpoints are unsuitable (fallback rate-limited to 2 req/min per IP per model).

Root problem: DSH rejects image attachments at the GUI/host admission layer when the active model is text-only (e.g. deepseek-v4-flash declares inputModalities: ["text"]), error MODEL_DOES_NOT_SUPPORT_IMAGES.
Common private-deployment setup: text-only main model + separate multimodal 'vision helper' (e.g. Qwen3.6-27B via llama.cpp) as an MCP server exposing describe_image(path).
MCP workaround works when given a file path, but the GUI attachment path never yields a reference the agent can see.
Feature suggestions: admission option for text-only models, modality override in model config, attachment reference exposure to the agent.

Alternative approach: Pilco-mmbridge turns a text-only model into a multimodal model without fine-tuning, pairing DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 with a separate vision model (e.g. Qwen3.5-9B-FP8-dynamic or Ornith-1.5-9B).
Runs both models on a 2x DGX Spark cluster; enables multimodal benchmarks with text-only LLMs.
Shows the broader ecosystem pattern: text-only brain + separate vision model is a recognized architecture.

stats.fact: dsh-vision-router has 1,093 GitHub stars (DSH Hub, updated 2026-09-09) and ~1,021 stars / 44 forks on the ysr666 repo.
The built-in anonymous OVHcloud vision fallback is capped at 2 requests/minute per IP per model; across 5 independent model buckets that is roughly 10 RPM in theory.
A free OVHcloud AI Endpoints access key lifts the same Qwen2.5-VL-72B-Instruct endpoint to 400 requests/minute per project per model (vs 2 anonymous).
The plugin provides 14 deep vision tools (15 with the privacy-gated vision_screenshot opt-in), covering Q&A, grounding, cropping, pixel diff, colors, OCR, SVG trace, cutout, and HTML screenshots.
Vision answers are cached by attachment content hash (default cacheTtlSeconds 3600, cacheMaxEntries 200), so later text turns substitute the recorded description without re-spending vision calls.
The pixel loop demo verified a UI rebuild at 2.54% final diff (32,939 / 1,296,000 differing pixels, threshold 16/channel) using vision_pixel_diff.
DSH rejects image attachments for text-only models at the admission layer with error MODEL_DOES_NOT_SUPPORT_IMAGES when inputModalities does not include 'image'.
Free-tier vision policies rotate: Cerebras retired its free tier in July 2026, SambaNova dropped to 20 requests/day, Hugging Face is $0.10/month.

angles: Routing bridge vs description bridge: most DSH vision plugins turn images into text descriptions (lossy, one-shot, blind to pixels); dsh-vision-router hands the image turn straight to a vision model (pixel-faithful) with a keyless free fallback.
DeepSeek stays the brain, vision model is only the eyes: text turns untouched in model, cost and context; image turns become ordinary tool-calling turns.
Image memory / visual memory: answers cached by content hash so the text-only agent genuinely remembers earlier images without re-spending vision calls — the 'visual memory' angle in the keyword.
Free out of the box: no API key, no Python, one command install; built-in OVHcloud anonymous fallback chain.
Verifiable pixel loop: reference -> vision_html_screenshot -> vision_pixel_diff -> fix -> repeat until mismatch converges; UI restoration becomes measurable instead of eyeballed.
Capability-aware auto routing with measured evidence, never inferred from model names; classified error failover (region/ToS/quota/rate-limit/context/network) with Retry-After-aware cooldown.
Stealth mode: optionally take over the official deepseek-official route so the model picker looks exactly like stock while each entry is an auto-vision wrapper.
Local-first privacy path: optional Ollama / LM Studio keyless offline vision backends for private, free, offline recognition.
